The artist Kristin Wiking creates kinetic sculptures, installations and video works, often using simple materials and mechanical or environmental forces to produce unexpected movement. Her practice is strongly influenced by humor, absurd logic, accidents and situations she cannot completely control For her 2026 exhibition Dog and Angel at SIC in Helsinki, Wiking removed or opened several of the gallery’s lower windows and installed a large sheet of thin plastic film inside the space.  There is no motor creating the movement. Wind, passing trains, cars and changes in the weather move the air through the building, causing the enormous surface to rise, fall, ripple and suddenly shake. The surrounding city effectively becomes the mechanism powering the sculpture. #asmr #calm #meditation #art #artist

Zhang Mingcong creates ink paintings directly inside water, replacing the traditional paintbrush with a syringe filled with specially prepared ink. Each drop blooms beneath the surface before slowly drifting downward. By carefully controlling its placement and movement, he builds flowing landscapes and detailed scenes inside the tank. The ink eventually settles onto paper at the bottom, preserving an image shaped by both the artist’s precision and the unpredictable movement of water. Because the ink never flows in exactly the same way twice, every finished painting is truly one of a kind. Artist: 明聪沙画 / 661265526 on Douyin #art #artist #painting #creative #satisfying
